title: Treasury Laws Amendment (2017 Measures No. 1) Bill 2017
short_title: Treasury Laws Amendment (2017 Measures No. 1) Bill 2017

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would correct tax concessions for investments held through trusts and simplify confidential information sharing between the Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) and the Commissioner of Taxation.
It would prevent certain exempt investment distributions from triggering capital gains consequences and allow ASIC to share information without its chairperson’s or delegate’s involvement.
For early stage company investments, the trust correction would cover payments directly from the investing trust, while existing tax secrecy protections would continue.
changes: The early stage investor correction would apply to capital gains events from 1 July 2017.
The venture capital correction would cover trust-interest payments in income years starting from 1 July 2016.
Authorised disclosures could include information ASIC obtained before the information-sharing amendment begins.
summary.affected: Trust beneficiaries investing in early stage companies or venture capital and ASIC would be affected.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Leigh
speeches.brief: Labor supported the Treasury Laws Amendment (2017 Measures No. 1) Bill 2017, which makes technical corrections to allow investors via interposed trusts to access capital gains concessions for start-ups and allows ASIC to share confidential information with the Tax Commissioner more easily.

speeches.speaker: Ed Husic
speeches.brief: The bill supports innovation by improving access to capital for startups, but the speaker warned that an ATO alert on the R&D tax incentive could restrict software development eligibility and harm digital startups, citing StartupAUS CEO Alex McCauley.
